whenAndWhere: A village of about four hundred people in late autumn, with a hall that takes sixty at a push, a shop that closes at one, and a house at the end of the lane with seven canvases in an upstairs room and a dehumidifier running. It is twenty-two years into a fifty-year instruction and everyone involved expects to be dead before it ends.
inTheAir: Estates that restrict access are now widely read as managing scarcity for value, because most of them are, and the assumption arrives before any evidence about a particular one.
An artist's instruction about their own work after death has no legal force beyond what an estate chooses to enforce, and estates are increasingly choosing not to.
The scholarship on any twentieth-century figure is now written from reproductions, so a body of work that has none is effectively outside the discipline and its absence is self-reinforcing.
Two academics have built partial readings of the work from letters and a single 1959 exhibition list, and those readings are now the work as far as anyone knows it.
Withholding has itself become a recognised way of generating interest, and everybody in the room knows that, including the niece.
contested: Whether a promise to a dead person can outrank the interest of people who are alive and want to see the work, and who will mostly be dead by 2048.
Whether the niece is keeping faith or has made the keeping of faith into her life's work and can no longer separate the two.
Whether the artist's instruction was a considered position about reproduction or the decision of a frightened person in her last year.
Whether marking the centenary at all is already a breach of the spirit of the thing, given that the will's evident purpose was to be left alone.
Whether the four institutions have honoured the condition or simply not had a reason to test it.
exhausted: An empty frame, or a blank rectangle at the proportions of a canvas, standing for a work not shown.
A veil, curtain or wrapping motif, which turns a legal instruction into a romance about mystery.
The artist's signature enlarged, which substitutes the one mark of hers that is not embargoed for all the ones that are.
A countdown to 2048, which makes the piece about waiting rather than about a decision.
Text from a letter set in a script face to signal intimacy and handwriting.
A silhouette of the house, or the studio window, standing in for the work by standing in for the place.

whoIsWatching.audience: A man of sixty-eight who delivered her groceries for nine years and never once saw a canvas, waiting for the bus outside the shop with eleven minutes to fill. He liked her. What he is deciding, without knowing he is deciding it, is whether she was a private woman or a difficult one, and the answer he settles on is the one the village will keep.
whoIsWatching.adversary: Not a person. The default reading, which is that any estate restricting access is protecting a price. It arrives instantly, it requires no evidence, and it is correct often enough that the audience is right to hold it.

transplants.ref: A sealed foundation deposit, placed under a building to be found only if the building is destroyed
transplants.why: Material deliberately made inaccessible for a stated duration, where the inaccessibility is the point of the deposit and not a side effect of where it was put.

transplants.ref: The closed period on state records, after which a file opens automatically
transplants.why: A withholding with an end date fixed in advance by rule rather than by whoever currently holds the material. The holder has no discretion, which is what distinguishes it from a refusal.

transplants.ref: A cast or squeeze taken from an inscription, which carries the form without the object
transplants.why: A derivation that is complete in one dimension and empty in every other. It is not a reproduction and it is not nothing, and the difference is procedural rather than visual.

transplants.ref: An inventory or probate list, which enumerates possessions without describing any of them
transplants.why: A record whose whole content is extent: how many, of what kind, in which room. It establishes that something specific exists while conveying nothing about it.

transplants.ref: The practice of covering mirrors and pictures in a house of mourning
transplants.why: Concealment carried out by the people closest to the thing, as an obligation rather than a choice, and lifted on a fixed day.

stakesLevelWhy: Nothing irreversible happens if this fails and nobody is harmed, but there is exactly one centenary, the person who has carried the promise is seventy-one, and a bad outcome starts the pressure to break the embargo twenty-two years early.
